Reclaim, throttling, high-work and over-high handler internals.
Victim scoring, termination and reaper mechanics beyond invocation points.
Cgroup and task iteration reference lifetime rules beyond observed acquire or release pairing.
Numeric values of batch sizes, retry limits, orders, flags and event enumerations.

findings.text: Task to group resolution tolerates a missing task and otherwise returns the memory group associated with the calling task context.
Kernel object charging first walks toward ancestors seeking a usable object group, then converts byte size upward to whole pages before debiting the owning group.

Memory event reporting increments local and hierarchical counters and wakes notification files, with hierarchical propagation disabled on older hierarchy mode or when local-only behavior is configured.
Task scanning visits every group in a subtree and applies a caller callback to each process, yielding periodically and stopping early with iterator cleanup on callback success.
Group maximum query combines the memory ceiling with a swap allowance bounded by global swap capacity, honoring whether combined accounting is enabled and whether swapping is permitted.
Page charging entry bypasses limits for the root group and delegates other groups to a richer routine that handles batching, reclaim, throttling and out-of-memory handling.

Charge attempts progress through cached stock use, batched limit acquisition, opportunistic reclaim and stock draining, bounded retries, conditional out-of-memory invocation, and finally either failure for ordinary contexts or forced over-limit admission for privileged or non-failing contexts.

System or group out-of-memory handling prefers already exiting culprits, avoids filesystem-less paths except for group pressure, classifies allocation constraints, optionally targets the allocator, then scans candidates and terminates a chosen victim or reports absence of killable tasks.

Available headroom is the smaller of memory and combined-space remainders when combined accounting applies, otherwise the memory remainder alone; zero is reported when any applicable ceiling is already reached.
Small object charges may be absorbed from per-cpu cached reserves keyed by owning object group; a cache hit with insufficient bytes fails rather than partially consuming.

After successful batched acquisition, unused surplus is returned to stock and groups above soft high thresholds request deferred user-return reclaim or throttling, with a synchronous over-high attempt when the caller can block and holds enough excess.

Victim eligibility treats the global init process and kernel threads as never killable, distinguishes group pressure from system pressure by presence of a target group, and treats a special negative order as a manual trigger.

Allocation constraint classification prefers group scope, then policy-restricted node sets, then cpuset restrictions, adjusting the considered total capacity accordingly and ignoring cpuset detail for very large orders or non NUMA builds.

Group out-of-memory serialization marks the whole subtree as under pressure, then attempts to claim every descendant guard; partial failure releases already claimed guards and reports contention, while success pairs with a matching release pass.

Older hierarchy out-of-memory preparation respects an administrative kill disable by parking the faulting context for later handling, otherwise records pressure state around the guarded notification step.

Observed group state includes hierarchical memory and combined counters with high and ceiling settings, swap accounting, per-node object groups, event counters and files, an out-of-memory waiter list plus subtree guards and pressure depth, and a deferred high-limit work item.

Charging must handle concurrent owner teardown yielding no task, reclaim recursion and exiting or already victimized callers, non-blocking contexts that cannot wait, and large orders that skip the killer path.
Group out-of-memory orchestration records the event, performs hierarchy-specific preparation, invokes the generic killer unless the size class is too large, and finalizes hierarchy state.
